rules.coverage_note: A class deriving from ModelAdmin or an inline is the admin presentation of a model.
The AppConfig subclass names an installed app and the directory it lives in.
get_wsgi_application()/get_asgi_application(): the module a server process loads.
A Form or ModelForm subclass is a bound input surface.
manage.py <stem>: the file name under management/commands is the command name.
A MiddlewareMixin subclass is request/response middleware; the modern callable spelling carries no marker and is not classified.
Each migrations/NNNN_*.py declaring class Migration is one step of an app's schema history.

migrations.CreateModel/AddField/RunPython ...: what one migration does to the schema. The receiver gate keeps a models.* call in the same file out, and the Migration end is minted here as well as by django.migration.
A class deriving from models.Model (or the shipped user bases) is a persisted model. Its id sorts first among the rules minting django:model:*, so these are the attributes that survive.
models.CharField(...) assigned in a class body: one column and its type. The receiver is what separates models.CharField from forms.CharField, so no models*.py path convention is needed.

admin.site.register(Author, AuthorAdmin) and @admin.register(Author): which model is exposed in the admin. The first argument's last segment is the model class, so the edge reaches the same django:model:* key the model's declaration mints.

models.ForeignKey("shop.Customer") / ForeignKey(Customer): the link between two models. call.arg0_name is the last dotted segment, so the "app.Model" string and the bare class name land on the same django:model:* key.
A module-level name in settings*.py is a Django setting; the edge says which settings module sets it. The value is not published by omega-python.
post_save.connect(on_author_saved, ...): the receiver names the signal and the first argument names the function, so both ends of handles are real names.

@receiver(post_save, sender=Author): which signal is listened for. The decorated function cannot be joined -- omega-python spans the decorator and the function as siblings -- so the handler is keyed by where it was written.
include("blog.urls"): which URLconf module this one mounts, named by its dotted module path.

path("orders/<int:pk>/", views.order_detail): the URL is the first argument, so the route is keyed by what it serves rather than by where it was written. A Django URLconf entry carries no HTTP method, so the method component is ANY. The view expression is an attribute, not an edge: see the .md.
re_path(r"^legacy/(?P<pk>\\d+)/$", ...): a regex is not a URL, so it stays out of the http:* key space and is keyed where it was written, carrying its pattern.
A class deriving from one of Django's generic views answers requests.
A non-underscore function in views*.py is a function view. Django puts no marker on one, so this is a path convention.
render(request, "orders/detail.html"): which template a view renders. The template name is the second argument; the glob on it keeps a non-literal argument out.

gaps: Python sources: the Django role of a declared class (model, view, form, admin, app config, middleware), the columns a model declares and whether each is scalar or relational and which model it points at, the URLconfs with the URL each path() serves and the module each include() mounts, the settings a settings module defines, the migrations of an app and the operations each runs, the management commands, the signals that are listened for, the templates a view renders and the WSGI/ASGI entry points are materialized.

omega-python publishes the first argument of a call (call.arg0, call.arg0_text, call.arg0_name) and the second as written (call.arg1_text) but no call.arg1_name, so Django's path(route, view) cannot name its view the way the view's own declaration does: the route carries the view expression as an attribute and no route->handler edge is emitted. See the .md, 'A field only the Pack can supply'.

omega-python spans reference.decorator on the decorator name and definition.function on the function_definition, which a decorated_definition encloses separately, so a decorator cannot be joined to the declaration it decorates; @receiver names its signal but not its handler, and @login_required and @admin.register cannot be attached to what they decorate.

A route's URL is the one written at its own path() call; Django composes the absolute URL from the prefixes of every include() above it, and include() spans no enclosing path() call, so a mounted route's absolute URL is not stated.
normalize_http_path folds :id, {id} and [id] but not Django's <int:pk>, so a Django route parameter is a distinct identity from the same parameter written in an Express or ASP.NET route.

The value of a setting is not published: definition.variable names INSTALLED_APPS, MIDDLEWARE, ROOT_URLCONF and ALLOWED_HOSTS but not their contents, so which apps are installed and which middleware is enabled remain not found.
Which class is a model, view, form, admin or app config is decided by its declared base; a class behind an indirect abstract base of the project's own is not classified.

reconciliation.v3_144: Pack/Framework fact contract reconciled against current host Pack; runtime-only/dynamic gaps remain explicitly bounded.
